pairs: Sum quidem et ego mortalis homo,
Certainly, I myself am also a mortal man,
et ex genere terreni illius qui prior factus est:
and the offspring of this earth, which was made beforehand;
et in ventre matris figuratus sum caro;
and in my mother’s womb I was fashioned with care,
decem mensium tempore coagulatus sum in sanguine:
within the time of ten months,
from the seed of man and the delight of sleeping together.
Et ego natus accepi communem aërem,
And when I was born, I drew in the common air,
et in similiter factam decidi terram,
and in similar fashion, I fell upon the earth,
et primam vocem similem omnibus emisi plorans.
and the first voice I uttered, like everyone, was crying.
I was nursed in swaddling clothes
nemo enim ex regibus aliud habuit nativitatis initium.
For none of the kings had any other beginning of birth.
Unus ergo introitus est omnibus ad vitam,
Therefore, there is only one entrance for everyone into life,
and understanding was given to me;
et venit in me spiritus sapientiæ:
and the spirit of wisdom came to me;
et præposui illam regnis et sedibus,
and I placed her before kingdoms and thrones,
et divitias nihil esse duxi in comparatione illius.
and I considered riches nothing in comparison with her.
Neither did I compare to her a precious stone,
quoniam omne aurum in comparatione illius arena est exigua,
for all gold in comparison with her is like a little sand,
et tamquam lutum æstimabitur argentum in conspectu illius.
and silver, in view of her, will be valued as if dirt.
Super salutem et speciem dilexi illam,
I loved her above health and beauty,
et proposui pro luce habere illam,
and I placed having her before light,
Venerunt autem mihi omnia bona pariter cum illa,
Yet all good things came to me together with her,
et innumerabilis honestas per manus illius;
and innumerable honors by her hand;
and I rejoiced in all these,
because this wisdom went before me,
et ignorabam quoniam horum omnium mater est.
although I did not know that she is the mother of them all.
This I have learned without falsehood
and her integrity I do not hide.
Indeed, she is an infinite treasure chest for men,
and those who make use of it,
become partakers in the friendship of God,
because they are recommended by the gifts of instruction.
Mihi autem dedit Deus dicere ex sententia,
Yet God has given to me to speak my mind,
et præsumere digna horum quæ mihi dantur:
and to conceive thoughts worthy of those things that are given to me,
because he is the leader of wisdom
In manu enim illius et nos et sermones nostri,
For in his hand are both we, and our words,
et omnis sapientia, et operum scientia,
and all wisdom, and the works of science,
Ipse enim dedit mihi horum quæ sunt scientiam veram,
For he has given me true knowledge of these things which exist:
so as to know the orderly arrangement of the world,
and the powers of the elements,
and the midpoint of the seasons,
and the orderly arrangement of the stars,
and the rage of wild beasts,
Et quæcumque sunt absconsa et improvisa didici:
and all such things as are hidden and unexpected, I have learned;
omnium enim artifex docuit me sapientia.
for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me.
Est enim in illa spiritus intelligentiæ,
For in her is the spirit of understanding:
humanus, benignus, stabilis, certus, securus, omnem habens virtutem, omnia prospiciens, et qui capiat omnes spiritus, intelligibilis, mundus, subtilis.
humane, kind, steadfast, trustworthy, secure, having all virtue, watching for all things and grasping all things with a pure and most delicate understanding of spirit.
Omnibus enim mobilibus mobilior est sapientia:
For wisdom is more active than all active things,
attingit autem ubique propter suam munditiam.
yet she reaches everywhere because of her purity.
For she is a breath of the virtue of God
et emanatio quædam est claritatis omnipotentis Dei sincera,
and a genuine emanation from the purity of the almighty God,
et ideo nihil inquinatum in eam incurrit:
and therefore nothing unclean can invade her.
Indeed, she is the brightness of eternal light,
et speculum sine macula Dei majestatis,
and the unspotted mirror of the majesty of God,
and the image of his goodness.
et in se permanens omnia innovat:
and, unchanging in herself, she renews all things,
et per nationes in animas sanctas se transfert;
and throughout the nations she conveys herself to holy souls,
establishing them as friends and prophets of God.
nisi eum qui cum sapientia inhabitat.
but those who dwell with wisdom.
For she is more spectacular than the sun,
and above the array of all the stars;
she is found to be before it.
but wisdom will not be overcome by malice.
